decisions.reason: As a simple care product tightly linked to the firm's installed base of wood floors, it fits existing technical knowledge and customer relationships, so management is likely to retain and refine it rather than withdraw it.

Maintenance oil builds directly on the firm's know-how in wooden floor surfaces and aftercare, and its several models give room for learning and adjustment through the firm's own R&D and installer feedback.

This care line is strongly related to the firm's established oiled-floor offer, so the firm should be able to interpret early market feedback and improve the range, even if overlap with other care products raises a small rationalisation risk.
A moisture-protection underlay complements the core flooring system and can be supported by the firm's technical guidance and channel knowledge, making continuation more likely than exit.

High-density underlay foam is adjacent to the firm's accessory business and benefits from existing flooring expertise, though as a more standardised add-on it faces a slightly higher chance of being dropped if uptake is weaker than expected.
An oak parquet line is very close to the firm's core competences in wood processing, design, and flooring sales, so absorptive capacity is high and the product is likely to stay on the market.
